name: Blue globe thistle
grown_as: A hardy perennial, by William's pond. His library gives Echinops ritro subsp. ruthenicus, about 0.9 m: a form with very narrow, glossy leaf lobes and bright steel-blue heads.
habit: An upright clump 60 to 90 cm high from a deep taproot. Stiff, branched, white-woolly stems, each branch ending in a ball-shaped head.

leaf.arrangement: A rosette at the base, then alternate up the stems
leaf.type: Simple but deeply cut (pinnately), nearly to the midrib, into narrow lobes
leaf.outline: Oblong to lance-shaped overall, 10 to 20 cm; lobes very narrow
leaf.base: Basal leaves narrowing to a short stalk; stem leaves stalkless and clasping
leaf.tip: Every lobe ends in a sharp spine
leaf.margin: Edged with small spines and rolled under
leaf.surface: Dark green and glossy above (sometimes faintly cobwebby); densely white-felted beneath
leaf.stalk: Short on basal leaves; none on stem leaves

flower.form: A perfect ball made of many tiny one-flowered heads packed together
flower.petals: Each tiny floret a slim tube with five narrow lobes curling back, so the ball looks like a cluster of small stars
flower.colour: Bright steel blue; metallic blue in bud
flower.centre: None: the whole ball is florets. Dark blue stamens stick out of the open florets
flower.behind: A few short, bristly bracts at the base of the ball, turned back
flower.carried: Alone at the tip of each stiff, white-woolly branch, upright

fruit: The ball dries to a brown-grey bristly sphere. Each seed is long and cylindrical, 6 to 8 mm, covered in silky pale hairs with a short crown of bristles.
seedling: Two oval smooth seed leaves. The first true leaves have wavy, spiny-toothed edges and are white beneath.
winter: Dies down to the crown. Dead stems with brown balls may stand; a few spiny rosette leaves may stay at the base.

leaf: leaf cut deeply into narrow pointed lobes
spines at the lobe tips and along the edges
dark green above, white felted beneath
bloom: perfect sphere of tiny star-like blue florets
no flat face and no ray petals
seed: long cylindrical seed covered in silky pale hairs
seedling: first true leaf spiny-edged and white beneath
young: rosette of deeply cut spiny dark green leaves, white beneath
flower: stiff upright branched stems each ending in one blue ball
seedhead: brown-grey bristly balls on dry stems
dormant: dead upright stems with brown balls, or cut back to the crown
a few spiny leaves at the base

look_alikes: Echinops bannaticus is taller with greyer-blue heads; Echinops sphaerocephalus is taller with grey-white heads. Sea hollies (Eryngium) have a collar of spiny bracts under a domed head. True thistles have flat-topped tufted heads, not balls.
